statement: For M equal-cost resolvable FOV locations with exactly K detectable-positive locations at arbitrary unknown support, the minimax probability of detecting at least one in b distinct queries is 1 - binom(M-K,b)/binom(M,b). Uniform sampling without replacement attains the value. Under the uniform K-subset prior, adaptive policies using only positive/negative results have the same average success probability.
assumptions: no side information correlated with target location
status: exact conditional model theorem; classical and not claimed new
novelty_boundary: Hypergeometric simple-random-sampling identity and exchangeability argument; no biological sample claim.
costs: One unit per FOV; real scout, stage, optical resolution, exposure, spectral-channel, storage, and analysis costs are handled separately.
falsifier: An adaptive strategy using only the stipulated binary outcomes and no location-correlated data exceeds the finite-population worst-case minimax value.
next_gate: For any proposed advantage, identify and validate the extra spatial prior, proxy, cluster prior, or post-positive follow-up interface.

statement: If L aggregate channels retain only independent Poisson totals with means given by the L integrated spatial intensity maps, then any two maps with equal per-channel integrals induce identical data laws; spatial organization cannot be tested from these totals alone.
assumptions: same integrated intensity in every channel
novelty_boundary: Identifiability statement for a specified aggregate Poisson interface; known general principle, not a claim about every spectroscopy instrument.
costs: Spatially resolved readouts or side information are outside the aggregate-only interface and must be charged if used.
falsifier: An aggregate-only measurement channel distinguishes two maps despite exactly equal complete observed intensity vectors and equal noise laws.
next_gate: Specify actual instrument outputs and determine whether any retained feature contains spatial labels or nonlinear spatial statistics.

statement: In the illustrative finite population (M_H,K_H)=(100,10), (M_L,K_L)=(900,1), scout cost 8 high-resolution-FOV equivalents, total budget 28, and minimum one confirmatory FOV per stratum, exact allocation (19,1) gives detection probability 0.8916076 versus 0.2694736 for uniform 28-FOV sampling at equal total cost.
assumptions: validated stratum map and calibration included in scout cost
status: exact finite computation from model assumptions; not biological evidence
novelty_boundary: A transparent conditional design comparison; not a new sampling algorithm or empirical claim.
costs: Scout, calibration, and scout analysis charged as 8 FOV equivalents; confirmatory acquisition uses the remaining 20.
falsifier: The exact combinatorial output differs when recomputed from the stated counts and allocations.
next_gate: Replace known counts with pilot uncertainty intervals and test on held-out specimens at matched end-to-end cost.

statement: Baker et al. model spatial FOV overdispersion by gamma-Poisson/negative-binomial and regional cell counts by beta-binomial, using pilot-estimated abundance/adjacency parameters; their results are model-conditioned and assume perfect marker-defined cell labels.
assumptions: as specified in cited paper and its datasets
novelty_boundary: Prior art for overdispersed spatial power analysis; does not supply a universal adaptive guarantee.
costs: Pilot data and spatial profiling assumptions are inputs; technical classifier error is not modeled as perfect ground truth.
falsifier: Full-text source contradicts the stated distributions or assumptions.
next_gate: Fit and validate the chosen overdispersion model on the intended specimen and technology.
